title: The Arm It Really Is: Calibrating the Table From Measured Tool Positions, What a Measurement Cannot Tell Apart, and How Many Poses Are Enough

questions.question: Why is the arm on the bench not its table?
options: Links and joint zeros are made to a tolerance, and every error is in the tool
questions.explanation: A third of a degree at the shoulder is millimetres at the tool.

questions.question: After calibrating, the error on poses it had not seen was:
questions.explanation: Down to the size of the noise.

questions.question: Fitted to only 4 poses, the error on others was:
options: 0.83 mm, though it was 0.00000000 mm on its own

questions.question: Moving joint 2's offset or joint 3's by 1 mm gave tool places that differed by:
What is the test of a calibration?
options: Its error on its own poses
Its error on poses it was not fitted to

questions.question: Why do the fitted corrections not have to be the true ones?
options: Some give the same tool place whatever the joints do, so the measurements cannot separate them
